title: Ensure 'Print Spooler (Spooler)' is set to 'Disabled'
remediation: Execute PowerShell command: Set-Service -Name Spooler -StartupType Disabled
reason: Disabling the Print Spooler (Spooler) service mitigates the PrintNightmare vulnerability (CVE-2021-34527) and other attacks against the service.

title: Ensure 'Windows Firewall: Private: Firewall state' is set to 'On (recommended)'
remediation: Set GP: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Windows Defender Firewall with Advanced Security\Windows Defender Firewall Properties\Private Profile\Firewall state to 'On (recommended)'
reason: If the firewall is turned off all traffic will be able to access the system, and a threat actor may be more easily able to remotely exploit a weakness in a network service.

title: Ensure 'Windows Firewall: Private: Inbound connections' is set to 'Block (default)'
remediation: Set GP: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Windows Defender Firewall with Advanced Security\Windows Defender Firewall Properties\Private Profile\Inbound connections to 'Block (default)'
reason: If the firewall allows all traffic to access the system, then a threat actor may be able to remotely exploit a weakness in a network service.

title: Ensure 'Windows Firewall: Private: Settings: Display a notification' is set to 'No'
remediation: Set GP: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Windows Defender Firewall with Advanced Security\Windows Defender Firewall Properties\Private Profile\Settings Customize\Display a notification to 'No'
reason: Firewall notifications can be complex and may confuse the end users, who would not be able to address the alert.

title: Ensure 'Windows Firewall: Private: Logging: Name' is configured
remediation: Set GP: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Windows Defender Firewall with Advanced Security\Windows Defender Firewall Properties\Private Profile\Logging Customize\Name
reason: If Windows Firewall events are not recorded it may be difficult or impossible for Administrators to analyze system issues or unauthorized activities of threat actors. Microsoft stores all firewall events as one file on the system (pfirewall.log). To improve logging, separate each firewall profile into its own distinct log file (e.g. privatefw.log).

title: Ensure 'Windows Firewall: Private: Logging: Size limit (KB)' is set to '16,384 KB or greater'
remediation: Set GP: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Windows Defender Firewall with Advanced Security\Windows Defender Firewall Properties\Private Profile\Logging Customize\Size limit (KB) to '16,384 KB or greater'
